title: Knowledge service (OKS)
description: Turns the knowledge service and data file declared by the session's workspace into seven native tools (search / references / info / check_intent / query / jaq_result / chart): find a key by name or description, walk the reference graph backwards from a key, read a node by key, validate a business question into named intents (the ones that pass come back with a key that the query must carry verbatim, and the tool re-hashes it before running), then answer it with real rows over a read-only connection. Each success is saved to a result file under the workspace's .data/, so the rows stay out of the model context until they are queried on demand with jaq_result, a jaq/jq expression over the row array. No model is baked in — a workspace opts in with an oks.json, and the agent explores the domain starting from the opaque key "index". Figures are drawn on the server into SVG files in the workspace: oks_chart takes its data from src (a saved query result, labelled "based on query results") or from data (rows you supply, "filled in by the agent"), and returns a markdown line that the agent puts into its reply to show the figure there. Three helpers ride along: time_now / time_calc for standard time representations and calendar arithmetic, and va_ask, which consults a vocabulary helper the plugin owns (a top-level agent on the same preset and workspace, sharing the process-wide index, archived while idle): it prepares that helper itself by putting role, the whole vocabulary and the working method into its system prompt — assembly sends no message at all — and, after every answer, collapses the question-and-answer into one fixed-text marker — so between questions the helper sees only vocabulary, method and the current question, while the session log stays append-only. The plugin writes into the workspace only those result files.
